title: `duckdb.create_function` type inferencing doesn't work with `from __future__ import annotations`
body:
### What happens?

In the Python UDF interface, `create_function` is able to infer types by inspecting the signature of the function to be registered. However, this doesn't work with [PEP 563](https://peps.python.org/pep-0563/) string annotations. The reason is [we use `inspect.signature`](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/0894f3d6ab1321619c40c5ef870ad252f16f83ab/tools/pythonpkg/src/python_udf.cpp#L282) which does not evaluate string annotations.

In Python 3.10+, [we can pass `eval_str=True`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/inspect.html#inspect.signature) to `inspect.signature` and it will parse the annotations for us. This has the disadvantage of potentially raising an exception or executing arbitrary code, but on balance, I think the user opts into this by registering a function without passing explicit types, and it is more useful than the current behavior in most cases.

### To Reproduce

```python
from __future__ import annotations
import duckdb

def foo(x: int) -> str:
    return str(x * 2)

duckdb.create_function("foo", foo)
```

This raises the following error:

```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "test.py", line 7, in <module>
    duckdb.create_function("foo", foo)
duckdb.duckdb.InvalidInputException: Invalid Input Error: Could not infer the return type, please set it explicitly
```

Removing the first line causes it to succeed.

title: Implement the Postgres timezone function
body:
The [timezone function](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/functions-datetime.html#FUNCTIONS-DATETIME-ZONECONVERT) is what the syntactic sugar of `AT TIME ZONE` translates to but we have not implemented it:

```sql
select now() at time zone 'europe/london' as start_time;
Error: Binder Error: No function matches the given name and argument types 'timezone(VARCHAR, TIMESTAMP)'. You might need to add explicit type casts.
    Candidate functions:
    timezone(TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE) -> BIGINT
    timezone(DATE) -> BIGINT
    timezone(TIMESTAMP) -> BIGINT
    timezone(INTERVAL) -> BIGINT
```

What it seems to do is either a) reinterpret a `TIMESTAMP`'s (UTC) bin values as values in the given zone and use them to produce a `TIMESTAMPTZ` or b) produce a TIMESTAMP whose (UTC) bin values are the same as the bin values of the `TIMESTAMPTZ`'s in the given zone.

Basically, it is a mechanism for encoding local time into instants. Which is sketchy but not hard to implement in ICU.

title: CTEs with `random()` should be materialised when referenced multiple times
body:
> [!NOTE]
>
> This might be working by design with the expectation that users "fix" this themselves with the `materialized` keyword. If this is the case, please close this issue immediately.

### What happens?

CTEs that use `random()` aren't necessarily materialised, so multiple references to a CTE that uses `random()` can have unintended consequences as the CTE might be re-computed in each use

Although [the docs do clarify the conditions for automatic CTE materialisation](https://duckdb.org/docs/sql/query_syntax/with.html#cte-materialization) (and using `random()` is not one of them), this might take users by surprise -- it sure did for me, at least 😄 

### To Reproduce

Here's a MWE:

```sql
with loop(x) as (select random())

select
    x as x_1,
    (select x from loop) as x_2
from loop
```

Although it was referenced multiple times, the CTE wasn't performing any grouped aggregation (which are [the conditions for automatic CTE materialisation](https://duckdb.org/docs/sql/query_syntax/with.html#cte-materialization)) -- so `x_1` and `x_2` have different values

This can, of course, be fixed by adding `materialized` to the CTE:

```sql
with loop(x) as materialised (select random())

select
    x as x_1,
    (select x from loop) as x_2
from loop
```

---

For comparison, this behaviour is different to both PostgreSQL and SQLite -- which are also different from each other!

- **SQLite**: `x_1` and `x_2` are equal by default. Using `not materialized` makes `x_1` and `x_2` different
- **PostgreSQL**: `x_1` and `x_2` are equal by default, and also when using `not materialized`

title: Relational API orders NAs first, how can we order them last?
body:
### What happens?

In the relational API, `rel_order()` does the same as `ORDER BY` in SQL -- `NULL`s are ordered first. How can we make them appear last, for compatibility with data frames?

### To Reproduce

``` r
library(duckdb)
#> Loading required package: DBI

df <- data.frame(a = c(1:2, NA))

dplyr::arrange(df, a)
#>    a
#> 1  1
#> 2  2
#> 3 NA

con <- dbConnect(duckdb())

rel <- duckdb:::rel_from_df(con, df)

exprs <- list(duckdb:::expr_reference("a"))

out <- duckdb:::rel_order(rel, exprs)
out
#> DuckDB Relation: 
#> ---------------------
#> --- Relation Tree ---
#> ---------------------
#> Order [a ASC]
#>   r_dataframe_scan(0x1104eb860)
#> 
#> ---------------------
#> -- Result Columns  --
#> ---------------------
#> - a (INTEGER)

duckdb:::rapi_rel_to_df(out)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 1
#>       a
#>   <int>
#> 1    NA
#> 2     1
#> 3     2
```

title: DuckDB v1.3 introduced a new error in read_csv related to date parsing.
body:
### What happens?

A CSV file that was previously parseable under v1.2 is no longer parseable under v1.3 because of an error trying to parse timezones. In addition, the `ignore_errors = true` flag appears to be ignored. 


### To Reproduce


Consider the following CSV taken from a much larger file: 

```csv
day_night,operation_no,flight_date_time
Night,38615452,2022/01/27 11:04:57 PM
Night,38615452,2022/01/27 11:04:57 PM
Night,38615475,2022/01/27 11:09:20 PM
```

Using the CLI with the following command: 

```sql
select * from read_csv('sample.csv');
```

Produces the following error: 

```
Not implemented Error:
Unknown TimeZone 'PM'!

Candidate time zones: "Pacific/Marquesas", "PLT", "PNT", "PRC", "GMT"
```

Setting `ignore_errors = true` results in the same error as above being generated: 

```sql
select * from read_csv('sample.csv', ignore_errors = true);
```

Setting `strict_mode = false` results in the same error as above being generated: 

```sql
select * from read_csv('sample.csv', strict_mode = false);
```

In DuckDB v1.2, this column was parsed as a VARCHAR and no error was reported. If DuckDB v1.3 is now "correct" it should still honour the `ignore_errors` options.

_This may be related to [Sniff Timestamp_TZ from CSV FIles #15730](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/pull/15730)_

title: Using the INTERVAL type
body:
One use case I'm trying to use duckdb for is to determine how many days have elapsed between two dates. The way I thought to do this was to first calculate `end_date - start_date`, but this leaves me with an INTERVAL type. Unfortunately, there do not appear to be any functions that act on INTERVAL types (I looked [here](https://duckdb.org/docs/sql/functions/date), and searched the codebase for functions on `interval_t`), and I wasn't able to cast an interval to a numeric type.

In Postgres, [`date_part` / `extract` work on the interval type](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/11/functions-datetime.html). I would be able to write `date_part('day', end_date - start_date)`.

Is this something you'd be willing to add to duckdb? I briefly looked into implementing it, but I'm not familiar enough with C++ and DuckDB's dispatch to immediately know how to approach it. With a little bit of guidance I'd be willing to contribute a patch, though!

title: Python enable_external_access config flag does not restrict csv/parquet access
body:
#### What happens?
Hi Folks!

One of my coworkers was testing out the enable_external_access config parameter that you added for us (thank you!). Unfortunately, it does not work like we had expected. It does correctly restrict access to DataFrames in the global scope, but it does not restrict file system access for csv or parquet files. We are completely open to a separate flag that would restrict file system access, or for that capability to be added to this flag - whichever is easier! We have other protections in place to isolate users and prevent them from accessing things we want to protect so this is not urgent or gating a deployment, but this would be a really great security feature for us.

Related prior issue: #1773

Thanks!
-Alex

#### To Reproduce
```python
import duckdb
import pandas as pd

dftest = pd.DataFrame([{"This":1,"is":2,"a":3,"test":4},{"This":5,"is":6,"a":7,"test":8}])
dftest.to_csv('test.csv')
file_creation_conn = duckdb.connect(':memory:', config={'enable_external_access': True})
file_creation_conn.execute("COPY (select * from dftest) to 'test.parquet' WITH (FORMAT PARQUET)").fetchdf()
file_creation_conn.close()

# The goal is to disable dataframe as well as filesystem access for this connection
conn = duckdb.connect(':memory:', config={'enable_external_access': False})

#The following statements succeed when they should fail:
df = conn.execute("select * from parquet_scan('test.parquet')").fetchdf()
print('parquet_scan results:\n',df)
df = conn.execute('select * from "test.parquet"').fetchdf()
print('test.parquet results:\n',df)
df = conn.execute("select * from 'test.csv'").fetchdf()
print('test.csv results:\n',df)
df = conn.execute("select * from read_csv_auto('test.csv')").fetchdf()
print('read_csv_auto results:\n',df)

#This statement correctly fails 
df = conn.execute("select * from dftest").fetchdf()
print('select * from dftest results:\n',df)
```

title: Control over Pandas type conversion
body: I was wondering if there is any way to control the type conversion with the Python client when converting results to a Pandas DataFrame. Specifically with columns of the [date](https://duckdb.org/docs/sql/data_types/date) type it looks like by default these are converted to Pandas `datetime64[ns]` when I would prefer a Pandas object column containing [Python `datetime.date`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#date-objects) values. This is is actually the default behavior if you do `conn.execute(...).arrow().to_pandas()` but I would like to avoid the intermediate Arrow conversion. Pyarrow exposes control over this with a [`date_as_object` flag](https://arrow.apache.org/docs/python/pandas.html#date-types). It would be nice if there were something similar for direct Pandas conversion.

title: [Python] Date -> NumPy/Pandas uses nanosecond precision
body:
### What happens?

Currently our conversion for a date-like type column from DuckDB -> NumPy array/Pandas column uses `datetime64[ns]`
```c++
	case LogicalTypeId::TIMESTAMP:
	case LogicalTypeId::TIMESTAMP_TZ:
	case LogicalTypeId::TIMESTAMP_NS:
	case LogicalTypeId::TIMESTAMP_MS:
	case LogicalTypeId::TIMESTAMP_SEC:
	case LogicalTypeId::DATE:
		dtype = "datetime64[ns]";
		break;
```

Internally we use microsecond precision for `TIMESTAMP[_*]` and days for `DATE`, so it makes much more sense to use `datetime64[us]` - which uses microsecond precision instead.

### To Reproduce

```py
>>> import duckdb
>>> df = duckdb.sql("select '2019-06-05'::DATE").df()
>>> print(df.dtypes)
CAST('2019-06-05' AS DATE)    datetime64[ns]
dtype: object
```

title: [httpfs] R2 secrets now require a 'REGION' to be provided
body:
### What happens?

In `1.0.0`, the following secret was enough to successfully import from an R2 bucket:

```sql
CREATE SECRET "r2_${bucketName}" (
    TYPE R2,
    ACCOUNT_ID '${accountId}',
    KEY_ID '${accessKeyId}',
    SECRET '${secretAccessKey}',
    SCOPE 'r2://${bucketName}',
    SESSION_TOKEN '${sessionToken}'
);
```

In `1.1.1`, attempting to import with this secret results in:

```
HTTP Error: HTTP GET error on '/${bucketName}/?encoding-type=url&list-type=2&prefix=${prefix}%2F' (HTTP 400)
```

Adding a `REGION` to the secret gets it working again:

```sql
CREATE SECRET "r2_${bucketName}" (
    TYPE R2,
    ACCOUNT_ID '${accountId}',
    KEY_ID '${accessKeyId}',
    SECRET '${secretAccessKey}',
    SCOPE 'r2://${bucketName}',
    SESSION_TOKEN '${sessionToken}',
    REGION: 'auto' 
);
```

### To Reproduce

Create an R2 bucket and applicable S3 secret. I've only tested with a session, scope, etc as seen above but guessing it should reproduce without.

Reason I say that is I'm guessing this is an inadvertent side-effect of #13167 (specifically https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/pull/13167/commits/c07dad437c721699ef5b005a3932a79a9bf0e97a), where the old default region was removed:

```diff
- empty_params.region = "us-east-1";
``` 

Note that [Cloudflare uses "us-east-1" as an alias for "auto"](https://developers.cloudflare.com/r2/api/s3/api/#bucket-region)

---

Create the secret

```
CREATE SECRET (
    TYPE R2,
    KEY_ID 'AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE',
    SECRET 'wJalrXUtnFEMI/K7MDENG/bPxRfiCYEXAMPLEKEY',
    ACCOUNT_ID 'your-account-id-here' -- your 33 character hexadecimal account ID
);
```

Attempt to import

```
SELECT * FROM 'r2://my-bucket/file.parquet';
```

title: Issue with "week" in date_add function
body:
### What happens?

When using the date_add function with the interval keyword "week," DuckDB throws a syntax error. This issue is specific to "week," as it works correctly with other keywords like "month."

### To Reproduce

1. Execute the following SQL query using DuckDB:

    ```
    SELECT date_add(INTERVAL 3 month, current_date);
    ```
    _Expected output: A date that is three months from the current date._
    
    Actual output: The query executes successfully, and the output is correct.

2. Execute the following SQL query using DuckDB:

    ```
    SELECT date_add(INTERVAL 3 week, current_date);
    ```
    _Expected output: A date that is three weeks from the current date._
    
    **Actual output: DuckDB throws a syntax error:**
    
    ```
    Parser Error: syntax error at or near "week"
    LINE 1: SELECT date_add(INTERVAL 3 week, current_date);
    ```

3. Execute the following SQL query using DuckDB as a workaround:
    
    ```
    SELECT date_add(INTERVAL '3 week', current_date);
    ```
    _Expected output: A date that is three weeks from the current date._
    
    Actual output: The query executes successfully, and the output is correct.

title: Support RENAME TABLE/VIEW while previous table/view is not cleaned up yet
body: Currently a `DROP` followed by a `RENAME` to the dropped entry in the same transaction fails because the mapping still contains the index pointing to the dropped entry. In order to fix this, the mapping in the `CatalogSet` needs to be transaction controlled as well, so multiple references to different tables from the same name can exist. See [this comment here](https://github.com/cwida/duckdb/pull/979#issuecomment-701993795) for more info.

title: INTERNAL Error: "Attempted to access index 1 within vector of size 1" when COPYing PLAIN_DICTIONARY STRUCT(LIST<STRUCT>) column with predicate pushdown
body:
## Summary

DuckDB 1.2.1 (latest nightly may also be affected; confirmed on 1.2.1 ARM64) raises an `InternalException` when using `COPY ... TO` on a query that:

1. Reads a `STRUCT(result LIST<STRUCT<...>>, ...)` column encoded with **PLAIN_DICTIONARY**
2. Applies a **predicate pushdown** (`WHERE id = X`) that selects the **first non-null row immediately after a large contiguous null block** (≥53,000 nulls) within a row group

## Minimal Reproduction

```python
"""
Minimal reproduction for DuckDB bug:
  INTERNAL Error: Attempted to access index 1 within vector of size 1
"""

import duckdb
import pyarrow.parquet as pq

REPRO_FILE = "repro_input.parquet"
OUTPUT_FILE = "repro_output.parquet"

# Step 1: Create trigger file
# Key conditions:
#   - Row group size >= ~120,000 rows
#   - Large contiguous null block (>=53,000 rows) in a STRUCT(LIST<STRUCT>) column, mid-row-group
#   - Target row is the FIRST non-null row immediately after the null block
#   - Enough distinct non-null values to trigger PLAIN_DICTIONARY encoding
setup_conn = duckdb.connect()
setup_conn.execute(f"""
COPY (
    SELECT
        i AS id,
        CASE WHEN i >= 59392 AND i < 112640 THEN NULL
        ELSE {{
            result: [
                {{label: 'illustration', confidence: 0.96}},
                {{label: '3d',           confidence: 0.02}},
                {{label: 'comic',        confidence: 0.01}},
                {{label: 'not_painting', confidence: 0.005}},
                {{label: 'bangumi',      confidence: 0.005}}
            ],
            label: 'illustration',
            confidence: 0.96
        }}
        END::STRUCT(result STRUCT(label VARCHAR, confidence DOUBLE)[], label VARCHAR, confidence DOUBLE) AS col
    FROM range(122880) t(i)
) TO '{REPRO_FILE}' (FORMAT PARQUET, CODEC SNAPPY, ROW_GROUP_SIZE 122880)
""")

pf = pq.ParquetFile(REPRO_FILE)
print(f"Encoding: {pf.metadata.row_group(0).column(1).encodings}")
# Verify: col encoding includes PLAIN_DICTIONARY

# Step 2: Show the misread (predicate pushdown silently returns wrong NULL)
conn1 = duckdb.connect()
v_wrong = conn1.execute(
    f"SELECT col IS NULL FROM '{REPRO_FILE}' WHERE id = 112640"
).fetchone()[0]

conn2 = duckdb.connect()
conn2.execute("PRAGMA disable_optimizer")
v_correct = conn2.execute(
    f"SELECT col IS NULL FROM '{REPRO_FILE}' WHERE id = 112640"
).fetchone()[0]

print(f"With optimizer (predicate pushdown): col IS NULL = {v_wrong}   ← wrong!")
print(f"Without optimizer (full scan):       col IS NULL = {v_correct}  ← correct")

# Step 3: Trigger the crash
conn3 = duckdb.connect()
try:
    conn3.execute(
        f"COPY (SELECT col FROM '{REPRO_FILE}' WHERE id = 112640) TO '{OUTPUT_FILE}'"
    )
    print("No crash (bug not triggered)")
except Exception as e:
    print(f"CRASH: {e}")
```

**Output:**

```
Encoding: ('PLAIN_DICTIONARY', 'RLE_DICTIONARY', 'RLE')
With optimizer (predicate pushdown): col IS NULL = True   ← wrong!
Without optimizer (full scan):       col IS NULL = False  ← correct
CRASH: InternalException: INTERNAL Error: Attempted to access index 1 within vector of size 1
```

## Root Cause (Two Layered Bugs)

### Bug 1 — Reader: Predicate Pushdown × PLAIN_DICTIONARY Dremel Decoder Misread

When DuckDB applies predicate pushdown to target a row immediately after a large contiguous null block in a `PLAIN_DICTIONARY`-encoded `STRUCT(LIST<STRUCT>)` column, the Dremel decoder **misreads the definition level at the null→non-null page boundary**, incorrectly marking the row as `NULL` at the outer struct level.

Evidence:

```sql
-- Returns NULL  (wrong — predicate pushdown active)
SELECT col IS NULL FROM 'repro_input.parquet' WHERE id = 112640;

-- Returns false  (correct — full scan, no pushdown)
PRAGMA disable_optimizer;
SELECT col IS NULL FROM 'repro_input.parquet' WHERE id = 112640;
```

Conditions that must all be met:
| Condition | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| Column encoding | PLAIN_DICTIONARY (legacy dict encoding) |
| Null block size | ≥53,000 contiguous nulls |
| Null block position | Mid-row-group (not starting at row 0) |
| Target row | **First** non-null row immediately after the null block |
| Row group size | ≥~120,000 rows |

### Bug 2 — Writer: `ListColumnWriter` Doesn't Guard Against Outer-NULL + Non-Empty Child Vector

After the misread above, the in-memory vector state becomes inconsistent:

```
outer_struct_vector[0].valid = false     ← misread as NULL by the reader
result_list_vector[0] = {offset, length=5}  ← child list still has 5 entries
child_vector.size = 1                    ← only 1 row allocated
```

`ListColumnWriter::Write` sums up `list_entry.length` for all rows (getting 5) and calls the child writer for 5 elements — but the child vector only has 1 row. `PrimitiveColumnWriter` then asserts `index < size` → crash.

The writer should skip child-field writes when the outer struct validity is `false`.

## Workaround

Use DuckDB to read, Polars to write — Polars' parquet writer handles this edge case correctly:

```python
result = conn.execute("SELECT * FROM read_parquet(...) WHERE ...").pl()
result.write_parquet("output.parquet")
```

Alternatively, `PRAGMA disable_optimizer` before the query avoids the misread but disables all optimizations.

## Environment

- DuckDB version: 1.2.1 (confirmed, ARM64; also reported on 1.4.3)
- Python: 3.13
- OS: Linux ARM64
- Install: `pip install duckdb`

title: Checkpointing is excessively slow, and gets slower with table size, when rows are large
body:
### What happens?

`CHECKPOINT` sometimes takes time proportional to the size of the table, especially when individual rows are more than a few kilobytes. For example, if I repeatedly insert 1,000 rows of 10,000 bytes each and then `CHECKPOINT`:
1. The first `CHECKPOINT` takes 3 seconds
2. The second `CHECKPOINT` takes 6 seconds 
3. The third `CHECKPOINT` takes 9 seconds
4. And so on

### To Reproduce

```python
import random
import duckdb
import pyarrow
import time
from pathlib import Path


def main(*, n_txns, n_rows_per_txn, n_bytes_per_row):
    db_file = Path("./ducktest.duckdb")
    if db_file.exists():
        db_file.unlink()
    db = duckdb.connect(str(db_file))
    db.execute("CREATE TABLE test (test VARCHAR)")
    for i in range(n_txns):
        data = pyarrow.table(
            {
                "test": pyarrow.array(
                    [random.randbytes(n_bytes_per_row) for i in range(n_rows_per_txn)]
                )
            }
        )
        t0 = time.monotonic()
        db.execute(
            """
            INSERT INTO test
            SELECT test
            FROM data
        """
        )
        t1 = time.monotonic()
        db.execute("CHECKPOINT")
        t2 = time.monotonic()
        print(f"execute={int((t1-t0)*1000)}ms checkpoint={int((t2-t1)*1000)}ms")
    db.close()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main(n_txns=100, n_rows_per_txn=1_000, n_bytes_per_row=10_000)
```

This prints something like:
```
execute=162ms checkpoint=2853ms
execute=232ms checkpoint=5995ms
execute=381ms checkpoint=9048ms
execute=228ms checkpoint=12221ms
...
```

(Oddly, if I set `n_bytes_per_row=1000` and `n_rows_per_txn=10000`, then it runs significantly faster, even though the total data is the same size. In that scenario, the pattern is that checkpoint time gradually climbs from about 200ms to about 2000ms over the course of about 10 repetitions, then drops back down to 200ms, and the pattern repeats.)

### What happens?

When importing a JSON file containing ISO 8601 date strings with 'T' separators into DuckDB, an error occurs during the parsing process. DuckDB seems to incorrectly infer the data type and attempts to parse these strings as timestamps using a format that does not match the actual string format.

### To Reproduce

1. **Generate the sample JSON data**:

   import json

   def generate_data():
       data = [
           {
               "createdAt": "2024-09-17T06:37:50Z",
               "updatedAt": "2024-09-17T06:37:50.000Z",
               "date": "2024-09-17",
               "resources": [
                   {
                       "interactions": [
                           {
                               "createdAt": "2024-09-17T16:37:46Z"
                           }
                       ]
                   }
               ],
               "templateValueStore": {
                   "f42af0a1-0231-4857-a0bb-5db7c5c9c266-0e2e0715-f339-443e-a927-cd1ec53591ef": "2024-09-17 16:37:46.367",
                   "f42af0a1-0231-4857-a0bb-5db7c5c9c266-ba82a466-24b4-441f-a000-66e203b50380": "2024-09-17 16:37:46.367",
                   "f42af0a1-0231-4857-a0bb-5db7c5c9c266-efab0a9d-58f2-4e84-a8f6-fab41d2fe6f2": "2024-09-17"
               }
           }
       ]
       with open("data.json", "w") as f:
           json.dump(data, f)

   generate_data()
   ```

2. **Attempt to read the JSON file into DuckDB**:

   ```python
   import duckdb

   try:
       # Attempt to read the JSON file into DuckDB
       result = duckdb.query("SELECT * FROM 'data.json'")
       print(result)
   except Exception as e:
       print("Error occurred:", e)
   ```

**Observed Behavior**:

An error is thrown when trying to read the JSON file:

```

DuckDB should not attempt to parse date strings with 'T' separators using a format that expects a space separator (e.g., `"%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S.%f"`). If the date string does not match the inferred timestamp format, DuckDB should either:

body:
### What happens?

QUALIFY ignores the alias that matches the original column name.

### To Reproduce

```sql
FROM VALUES (1), (2) AS t(n)
SELECT lead(n) OVER() AS n
QUALIFY n IS NOT NULL;
```
or same with prefix alias:
```sql
FROM VALUES (1), (2) AS t(n)
SELECT n: lead(n) OVER()
QUALIFY n IS NOT NULL;
```
returns:
```
┌───────┐
│   n   │
│ int32 │
├───────┤
│     2 │
│  NULL │
└───────┘
```
Expected result, as in query where alias non-matched with column name:
```sql
FROM VALUES (1), (2) AS t(n)
SELECT lead(n) OVER() AS n1
QUALIFY n1 IS NOT NULL;
```
```
┌───────┐

title: Queries with list_aggregate and unnest on same list value slow and memory-intensive; DuckDB should optimize by calculating the aggregate before unnesting.
body:
### What happens?

A SELECT that applies `list_aggregate` and `unnest ` on the same list-typed value is very slow and memory-intensive. A rewrite (extra cte) that forces execution of the aggregate computation so it happens prior to unnesting operation is very much faster.

This suggests DuckDB re-executes the aggregation operation for each row generated by the unnesting operation. The request is to optimize such queries so that the list_aggregation is executed no more often than necessary.

### To Reproduce

Slow query:

```sql
with data as (
    SELECT range(100000) as arr
), cte1 as (
  SELECT list_aggregate(arr, 'COUNT') as arr_count
  ,      list_aggregate(arr, 'AVG')   as arr_avg
  ,      unnest(arr)
  FROM data
)
select * 
from cte1;
```

Equivalent fast query:

```sql
with data as (
    SELECT range(100000) as arr
), cte1 as (
  SELECT list_aggregate(arr, 'COUNT') as arr_count
  ,      list_aggregate(arr, 'AVG')   as arr_avg
  ,      arr
  FROM data
), cte2 as (
  SELECT arr_count
  ,      arr_avg
  ,      unnest(arr)
  FROM cte1
)
select * 
from cte2; 
```

title: "Implicit any" when accessing a remapped key of a mapped type (but no error when accessing the whole mapped type)
Enums as generics fail to be imported in declaration output
body:
<!-- Please try to reproduce the issue with `typescript@next`. It may have already been fixed. -->
**TypeScript Version:**  3.2.0-dev.20181017

<!-- Search terms you tried before logging this (so others can find this issue more easily) -->
**Search Terms:** enum declaration generic type argument import

When a field/variable is set via its value, and the value's type contains an enum as a type argument, the enum is not imported in the declaration for that file. This is kind of confusing to explain, so I'll make it more clear with the following example:

### Code

**TestEnumAndClass.ts**
This file creates the enum and a few things which use the enum as a generic.

```ts
export enum TestEnum {
	Foo,
	Bar,
	Baz
}

export default class GenericClass<T extends TestEnum = TestEnum> {
	public constructor(test: T) {}
}

export type GenericType<T extends TestEnum = TestEnum> = Array<T> | IterableIterator<T> | Set<T> | Map<T, T>;

export const genericInstance = new GenericClass(TestEnum.Foo);
export let genericArray: GenericType<TestEnum.Foo>;
```

**test.ts**
This file imports some of the things using the enum as a generic, but not the enum.

```ts
import GenericClass, { genericInstance } from "./TestEnumAndClass";

export const tests = {
	foo: genericInstance,
	bar: {} as any as GenericClass,
	baz: genericArray,
	fizz: {} as any as GenericType
};

export const buzz = genericInstance;
```

### Expected behavior:
The enum should be imported, since it's required to correctly type the variables. If not imported this way, imported via an inline `import()` call.
```ts
// test.d.ts
import GenericClass, { GenericType, TestEnum } from "./TestEnumAndClass";
export declare const tests: {
    foo: GenericClass<TestEnum.Foo>;
    bar: GenericClass<TestEnum>;
    baz: GenericType<TestEnum.Foo>;
    fizz: GenericType<TestEnum>;
};
export declare const buzz: GenericClass<TestEnum.Foo>;
```

### Actual behavior:
The enum is not imported at all. This causes the declaration file to be invalid.
```ts
// test.d.ts
import GenericClass, { GenericType } from "./TestEnumAndClass";
export declare const tests: {
    foo: GenericClass<TestEnum.Foo>;
    bar: GenericClass<TestEnum>;
    baz: GenericType<TestEnum.Foo>;
    fizz: GenericType<TestEnum>;
};
export declare const buzz: GenericClass<TestEnum.Foo>;
```

https://www.typescriptlang.org/play/?ts=5.9.0-beta#

### 💻 Code

```ts
declare function getNum(): Promise<number>;
declare function getStr(): Promise<string>;
declare function useTuple(tuple: [number, string]): void;
const p = Promise.resolve([]).then(() => Promise.all([getNum(), getStr()])).then(useTuple);
```


### 🙁 Actual behavior

The `Promise.all` infers to `Promise<(number|string)[]>`.

### 🙂 Expected behavior

The `Promise.all` should infer `Promise<[number, string]>`.

### Additional information about the issue

This only happens when the `Promise.all` call is directly returned.  If I instead write

```
const p = Promise.all([getNum(), getStr()]);
return p;
```

then it infers the tuple correctly again, even without doing anything that would suggest it should infer the type differently.

This PR also impacted inference of enums: in [another example](https://www.typescriptlang.org/play/?ts=5.9.0-beta#-EEeLygHq5RxszlDHmUPm9IUGVxIhSgAB6H1BGy2SF2YmhOFh8OlGDFLCAA), I pass `{mode: new Subject(Mode.A)}` into a function that fails because it infers `Subject<Mode.A>` while if I save a temporary `const mode = new Subject(Mode.A);` then it infers `Subject<Mode>` and passes.

**TypeScript Version:**  3.4.3

<!-- Search terms you tried before logging this (so others can find this issue more easily) -->
**Search Terms:**

**Code**

```ts
Array.prototype.flatMap = function(f, that?) {
  // infer U
  type ElementType<T> = T extends readonly any[] ? T[number] : T
  type U = ElementType<ReturnType<typeof f>>
  // polyfill
  const ys: U[] = []
  this.forEach((x, i, xs) => {
    const y = f.call(that!, x, i, xs)
    Array.isArray(y) ? ys.push(...(y as U[])) : ys.push(y as U)
  })
  return ys
}
```

**Expected behavior:**

This an umbrella issue. I ran into multiple issues trying to polyfill `Array#flatMap` without duplicating the type signature from `"lib": ["esnext"]`:

```ts
interface Array<T> {
    flatMap<U, This = undefined> (
        callback: (this: This, value: T, index: number, array: T[]) => U|ReadonlyArray<U>,
        thisArg?: This
    ): U[]
}
```

**Actual behavior:**

1. `ReturnType<typeof Array.prototype.flatMap>` types as `{}[]`.
2. `ElementType<ReturnType<typeof f>>` types as `U | ElementType<U>` instead of unifying on `U`.
3. `f.call(that, x, i, xs)` errors with `Argument of type 'This | undefined' is not assignable to parameter of type 'This'.`.
4. Type guards don't appear to work in `Array.isArray(y) ? ys.push(...y) : ys.push(y)`. The inferred types are `(U | readonly U[]) ? (any[]) : (U | readonly U[])`. I suspect it has to do with `readonly`.

title: No Error for use before def in property initializer
Feature request: Meta-Programming Hooks / Active Decorators
body:
# Problem

Currently meta-programming with TypeScript is not ideal. There are a lot of features which support meta-programming but there is a lot of room for getting better.
This feature request targets code generation based on rules/declarations and meta information.

I've written [pretend](https://github.com/KnisterPeter/pretend) and realized that its not syntactically good to use decorators (as meta-information) to drive code generation.  
But it could be quite intuitive for developers to do so.  
The current limitations are the following:

* Interfaces could not be target for decorators
* Classes (which could be decorated) must have methods with body, but the body is not necessary since it is generated and only target for the meta-data
* Empty method bodies with return types are considered failure for linters and the tsc
* Even if interfaces could be decorated, they are not part of the emitted code (which is okay)

# Solution / Idea

Allow for decorating interfaces.  
Probably not only interfaces but a syntactic extension (e.g. `#decorator()`) to annotate other code as well (e.g. class properties, functions, variables, ...)

These decorators could then be used as hooks into the tsc code emitter and drive code generation.
With this feature meta-programming would get a lot gain, since valid typescript code could be annotated and valid js-code could be emitted. E.g. Interfaces could generate classes.

Something like [active annotations like in xtend](http://www.eclipse.org/xtend/documentation/204_activeannotations.html) would be a good start.

If this idea would be considered acceptable I would be glad to contribute more examples and better explanations.

title: Add a flag to specifically disallow the "lazy initialization of an empty object" pattern in checkJs mode
body:
# Bug Report

### 🔎 Search Terms

ts2739 jsdoc 

### 🕗 Version & Regression Information

- This is the behavior in every version I tried, and I reviewed the FAQ for entries about `ts2739`

### ⏯ Playground Link

Playground links with relevant code:
 - [JavaScript + JSDoc](https://www.typescriptlang.org/play?strictNullChecks=true&noUncheckedIndexedAccess=true&noUnusedLocals=true&noUnusedParameters=true&noFallthroughCasesInSwitch=true&useUnknownInCatchVariables=true&exactOptionalPropertyTypes=true&noImplicitOverride=true&noPropertyAccessFromIndexSignature=true&ts=4.7.2&filetype=js#code/PQKhCgAIUgBAXAngBwKYBNUDNIDED2+UMsyATvmmUpAN4B2ArgLYBGqZAvpFocXOUocatAM7wyAS3oBzbqwCGZYsHDhQJJGjoF83EKoDG+euMgAPSAF46nANyRgwSADl8kDhTKQAFh1QANB4Abqj0kPA++IwyPhaQkqKQzImi0jKQovjMqJCCVPCSqKLg5gB0vO42AMx24EA)
 - [TypeScript equivalent of the same code](https://www.typescriptlang.org/play?#code/C4TwDgpgBAYg9nKBeKBvAUFLUBmCBcUAdgK4C2ARhAE4Dcm2FAhtYQM7DUCWRA5vQF906AMZwiHKAA8oheIhSoBtKAHpV0qLwjA2UJlAAqAZQBMAdgDMATig1qcagBp9eiFMgjgEACbopAHR4ClCW9EA)

### 💻 Code

**JavaScript**
```js
/**
 * @typedef Foo
 * @property {number} foo
 * @property {string} bar
 */

/** @type {Foo} */
const x = {}; // No error here, even though x is missing some properties
x.foo = 3;
```

**TypeScript**
```ts
type Foo = {
    foo: number;
    bar: string;
}

const x : Foo = {}; // x gets a TS2739 error, as expected
x.foo = 3;
```

### 🙁 Actual behavior

The JavaScript + JSDoc version doesn't get a TS2739 error.

### 🙂 Expected behavior

TS2739 is emitted, similar to what happens in the TypeScript equivalent of this code.

I reckon this might have been added to solve a situation that might occur in JavaScript that will never happen when using TypeScript only (although I'm not sure what that situation might be). If that's the case, consider this a feature request to add a configuration option that removes this behaviour 🙂.

title: Callsite inference of a conditional string literal type fails when the literal type of the parameter would produce a valid expansion
body:
This is a bit of a weird one, bear with me...

As a hobby project/exercise, I've been working on (parts of) a literal regex engine using recursive TypeScript types.  It is flatly impossible to do much of interest along these lines with first-class types, so instead I've been using conditional types to write validators that either resolve to `never` or to identity.  This allows validation of literal function params, like a sort of SFINAE:

```typescript
// this type can only be inferred to nonempty values
type NonEmpty<S extends string> = S extends "" ? never : S;
// we cannot call this with an empty string literal unless we intentionally lie to TSC about the type
function onlyAcceptsNonEmpty<S extends string>(param: NonEmpty<S>) ...
```

While mucking around with this, I found myself in a situation where TSC fails to infer such a parameter type in situations where the literal type of a provided string literal argument produces a valid expansion.  Instead, it falls back to the broader string type, which fails to expand.

I've extracted a repro case [here](https://www.typescriptlang.org/play/?#code/C4TwDgpgBAkgdgYwDYFcAmEDOAeAyigI02ACcBLOAcyggA9gI41MpjyqA+KAXigAMAJAG82FSgF9h+IqTGSRsquL4BuAFBrQkKAEUUAQzjAyAMzIQSPKACIAVNagAfGwGpr6zeGh7DxsxDQreGR0LGwfI1NzEg4PLWgAOQB7YAi-czQ8GnpGZlZFSi5eXGyGJhY0qIC1KCgAfig4CAA3CxqoAC4oXDivKGS4AFEAWzBQLLoyvNFOKxLJ3JZrBwam1ssuns9tABEySjJgCZzy-PZCnnb5k7zBIQGRsZBsChMLKAAFEggzWg55V7vABKWGAynatQaIOIpUW-GED1G40BlnwJl+-z4ENq9UaLTaOJxm2xXTWFl62gGAFl9MAEAALMRo37YdoAYXp+ksC1OM0oABorrDeQVBUVusLbsI9gcjhyuf9hCjuih0WRaODIf0knAaXTGVRmersPKSPyVWq-u1NhToEbaAB5EzHKYsPlFIU8vIyw54DjYhq4EkSr0sO6Ip4vOBvSxfH7qxX3HWPZHR972zHYrUlZz2pwW35OvCqjFZzp49a2qAAGX0xB9R2urrOYnFDeLlqLuA4sQ08Sg0KSSFaAC0LEkHSQqUlvqzanHfpK3aKriX1UuW1RBbU9QyN3ztyGbsvzmKrAv16H4UJlXGLxrhLX6-tfffM1rd-SN3d7wC05ZoTBLFCShLAh1aSp-BIHAy1qe1D0JWpqVpBkmTXWhsCfYB2zfc1AI4BDEKDRCoH9Qkuk-b9hDvb5fj-GMB1BTVENAzBwIgSDohgkjCXg2CcWQ-U0MtTC62wl8jlwxjiAI-i4P4sjENJfESGtCtyT7PpB2HDiDEiKDuMYyg6H3FcdxQr8rwPT1j03aheE-M9eBBYzaCopNUj09IAijBi33kTiLHo9N0OY0DXPc39bCkULgJxVj2LHEgJynGcIGwe9zXgqBHO6RTamU9Y1Moq8XLoANumDMkSA8EwUEQYwdSgBhiBdOF3QACnaMAuX0YYum0iCvKqaDsGsWh9FsAh7Cy2SAEooCEcQ+1BDrxv0AhNs26w5vUFqjnWrbto4NaJqOggdvUIA).  Curiously, the behavior depends on the order of the recursive branches in the parameter type; if we swap the success check to the beginning of the type, [the inference works as expected](https://www.typescriptlang.org/play/?#code/C4TwDgpgBAkgdgYwDYFcAmEDOAeAyigI02ACcBLOAcyggA9gI41MpjyqA+KAXigAMAJAG82FSgF9h+IqTGSRsquL4BuAFBrQkKAEUUAQzjAyAMzIQSPKACIAVNagAfGwGpr6zeGh7DxsxDQreGR0LGwfI1NzEg4PLWgAOQB7YAi-czQ8GnpGZlZFSi5eXGyGJhY0qICoAH4oOAgANwsoAC4oXDivKGS4AFEAWzBQLLoyvNFOKxKx3JZrBzqG5st2zs9tABEySjJgUZzy-PZCnjUoDtK5--6G3u1KLZ6rV7DFZHT2rhFWazsPdf0aC6lvaefhNffmGAUDUxre0wftmkqfwSBwZMjS1bddRNbA72AFsnyNSFgA4I0Oz9N8d3FQNPw+L8FR-SxUP-ME6khYCIFA6IcCLNNIPorFoJ1Khk3g6tEIffZkMAtD9zTMFfUEi4vUEksVjNepSxJbtukogdqIMSIwLoi5AUoOhd0XTdtRwgM115F1cMMqxsJFM5dO3VdklSZT0gCbANLoMTyI6P1nJXEygxSGjHMvD40XkPySG-cMc1VMiAM8j8hC-WwpGXKK3IUocRzHCcp2vDDlyNcyOlc8TpMkoriQ8EwUEQYw4ygBhiHta4nQACjAdl9AGdpUqU3wqnA7BrFofRbAIewMI4ABKKAhHEbsgSagb9AIJaluscb1Dq-YFuWlaOHmwbtoIVb1CAA).

The relevant change between the two:

```typescript
// this does not work for callsite inference
type ResolveQuantifiers<
  Regex extends string,
  Match extends string,
  S extends string = Match,
> = Regex extends `${NotQuantified<infer Prefix>}${Quantifier}${infer Suffix}`
  ? Regex extends `${Prefix}*${Suffix}`
    ? ResolveZeroOrMore<Prefix, Suffix, Match, S>
    : never
  : Match extends Regex
    ? S
    : never;

// this works for callsite inference
type ResolveQuantifiers<
  Regex extends string,
  Match extends string,
  S extends string = Match,
> =
  Match extends NotQuantified<Regex>
    ? S
    : Regex extends `${NotQuantified<infer Prefix>}${Quantifier}${infer Suffix}`
      ? Regex extends `${Prefix}*${Suffix}`
        ? ResolveZeroOrMore<Prefix, Suffix, Match, S>
        : never
      : never;
```

Note that in both cases, the `ResolveQuantifiers` type itself seems to behave as we would like, and if we provide a copy of the parameter as an explicit generic argument the compilation error goes away.

This seems like an unintended and undesirable behavior.  Naively, I'd expect the inference engine to check the exact literal type of a literal parameter *first*, and infer the resulting generic if it evaluates to something other than `never`.  What's going on here?

  https://www.typescriptlang.org/dev/bug-workbench/

  As a last resort, you can link to a repo, but these will be slower for us to investigate.
-->
[Playground link with relevant code](https://www.typescriptlang.org/play?#code/DYUwLgBAHlBcEDsCuBbARiATgbgFC4migDowB7AMQEsoQATACgEo8B6ViAPQH5d2IwATwAOIMgDMiEALyzEqDJgiAZcnyhIgwQEJ4ydFjwEIm0pRr1mbDjz4choiccEy5exRECg5EA)

### 💻 Code

<!-- Please post the relevant code sample here as well-->
```ts
let xx: number;

  xx.toFixed();
// ^?
// typeof xx === number ❌

let yy!: number;

  yy.toFixed();
// ^?
// typeof yy === number ✅
```

### 🙁 Actual behavior

<!-- What happened, and why it was wrong -->
TS reports the type of the used-before-assigned variable `xx` as `number`, and reports error `Variable 'xx' is used before being assigned. (2454)`

### 🙂 Expected behavior

<!-- What you expected to happen instead, and why -->
TS reports the type of `xx` as `number | undefined`.

### Additional info

This behaviour makes it difficult for us to write lint rules because when we attempt to check if the variable is `undefined`, the type system reports that it is not.

Examples:
- checking for unnecessary conditions based on types
    - `if (xx != null) {}` The types say `xx` is `number`, so `!= null` looks like it's unnecessary.
- checking for unnecessary type assertions
    - `xx!` Again the types say `xx` is `number`, so the non-null assertion looks like it's unnecessary.

Example issue:
- https://github.com/typescript-eslint/typescript-eslint/issues/453
- https://github.com/typescript-eslint/typescript-eslint/issues/6640

[In the past we've manually coded up logic to do used-before-assigned checks](https://github.com/typescript-eslint/typescript-eslint/blob/a1a20b3fd12ce47d3c98fea53314ea14b42eeec1/packages/eslint-plugin/src/rules/no-unnecessary-type-assertion.ts#L91-L125) where necessary - but it's pretty gnarly code to maintain and we have to ensure that we cover this case in our implementation.

It would be great if TS reported the "correct" type here with `undefined`.

  * Read the FAQ: https://github.com/Microsoft/TypeScript/wiki/FAQ

Please fill in the *entire* template below.
-->

<!-- Please try to reproduce the issue with `typescript@next`. It may have already been fixed. -->
**TypeScript Version:**  3.0.0-dev.201xxxxx

<!-- Search terms you tried before logging this (so others can find this issue more easily) -->
**Search Terms:** 

**Code**

```ts
interface Collection<T> {
  elems: T[];
}
interface CollectionStatic {
  new <T>(): Collection<T>;
}
declare const Collection: CollectionStatic;

const ALL = "all";
type All = typeof ALL;

const result: Collection<All> = new Collection();
```

**Expected behavior:**
No errors.

**Actual behavior:**
```
Type 'Collection<string>' is not assignable to type 'Collection<"all">'.
  Type 'string' is not assignable to type '"all"'.
```

`typeof ALL` copies the type of the ALL const - in this case, that is a _widening_ literal "all", which is then, during return type inference for `Collection`, _widened_, causing the assignment of the resulting inference to fail. Intuitively, widening types aren't exposed syntactically and aren't simple to understand, and typically they only result from expression positions. `typeof` currently breaks that and copies a widening type into a type position where it behaves unexpectedly. The fix, IMO, is simple: `typoef` should strip freshness.

This issue cropped up due to a lib change (we removed a bogus no-arguments-result-in-`any` overload on `Map` and replace it with generic defaults) that exposed the error in an RWC test.

# Suggestion

differing accessor types

## ✅ Viability Checklist

My suggestion meets these guidelines:

* [x] This wouldn't be a breaking change in existing TypeScript/JavaScript code
* [x] This wouldn't change the runtime behavior of existing JavaScript code
* [x] This could be implemented without emitting different JS based on the types of the expressions
* [x] This isn't a runtime feature (e.g. library functionality, non-ECMAScript syntax with JavaScript output, new syntax sugar for JS, etc.)
* [x] This feature would agree with the rest of [TypeScript's Design Goals](https://github.com/Microsoft/TypeScript/wiki/TypeScript-Design-Goals).


## ⭐ Suggestion

<!-- A summary of what you'd like to see added or changed -->

#42425 forces the getter type to be assignable to the setter type. This makes the feature limited on the following DOM typing case, and thus it could be great if the limitation can be lifted.

## 📃 Motivating Example

```webidl
[Exposed=Window]
interface CSSStyleRule : CSSRule {
  attribute CSSOMString selectorText;
  [SameObject, PutForwards=cssText] readonly attribute CSSStyleDeclaration style;
};
```

```ts
interface CSSStyleRule extends CSSRule {
    selectorText: string;
    get style(): CSSStyleDeclaration;
    set style(cssText: string); // currently an error
}
```

```ts
document.body.style = "display: none" // thus still an error while the actual behavior allows it 🤔
```

## 💻 Use Cases

Allows Web IDL readonly attributes to be assignable, and thus the DOM typing better matches the actual behavior.

body:
### Description

In a long running Docker instance it is possible to get orphan entries in /var/lib/docker/overlay2 that do not clear up when `docker system prune -af` or similar commands are issued.

How to create these overlay2 orphan entries?
- Provision a large (100GiB+) volume for /var/lib/docker
- Deploy a gitlab runner agent and let your developers go wild.
- Realise that between docker never releasing images without explicit prunes, and Developers insatiable lust for resources, no particular volume allocation can ever actually account for the disk space requirements of builds.

**Use Case**
For the purpose of CI/CD, I'd like be able to `bind mount` docker socket from Docker host into container under a different user (other than root) and specific permission. This lets us use docker from inside the Docker container for various CI/CD tasks as a user other than root.

I expect something like running `docker run -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock/:<user>:<group>:<perm>`

Related to [#2259](https://github.com/moby/moby/issues/2259) but this one is a more specific case - it only deals with `bind mount` (not volume)

title: debian init scripts are a little race-y
body:
Short repo: On debian, run the following commands:

```
# service docker stop
[ ok ] Stopping Docker: docker.
# service docker start ; service docker start
[ ok ] Starting Docker: docker.
[ ok ] Starting Docker: docker.
# docker ps
2014/06/03 15:59:30 Cannot connect to the Docker daemon. Is 'docker -d' running on this host?
```

Long explanation: I'm installing docker with salt and have the following in my .sls file:

```
docker-repo:
  pkgrepo.managed:
    - humanname: Docker Repo
    - name: deb https://get.docker.io/ubuntu docker main
    - key_url: https://get.docker.io/gpg

lxc-docker:
  pkg.latest

docker:
  service.running:
    - enable: True
    - require:
      - pkg: lxc-docker
```

What is happening here is the following:
- The package is getting installed with `apt-get install` and the docker daemon is started with the init script.
- The init script returns as soon as the docker process is started.  No pid file is written.
- Salt, via `service.running` calls `service docker status` to see if the daemon is running.  Because the pid file hasn't been written it says 'no, not running'.
- Salt then wants to make sure the service is running so it runs `service docker start`
- This starts a second process.  But there is already a process running that hasn't written a pid file.  The end result is a wedged docker that doesn't respond to the API.

How to solve this?  
1. If docker was able to really daemonize itself, it could write out the PID file and then have the original host process exit.  Then `start-stop-daemon` wouldn't use the --background option.
2. Change the init script to not match based on pid file and instead use the executable name option.  That has the side effect of killing client invocations in addition to the server daemon.
3. Have `start-stop-daemon` write and manage the pid file instead of docker.

title: Proposal: DAG image builder (can execute muti-stage build in parallel)
body:
## Proposal

Beginning from 17.05, Docker supports "multi-stage" Dockerfile.

My proposal is to convert such Dockerfile to DAG internally, and execute it in parallel.

![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/9248427/24951034/00b9326c-1fae-11e7-8ade-c9956e3f0693.png)

No change to file format nor UX

POC is available: https://github.com/docker/docker/pull/32402

## Tasks

### Implement generic DAG utility

I made a small generic DAG package: https://github.com/AkihiroSuda/go-dag

```go
import (
    "github.com/AkihiroSuda/go-dag"
    "github.com/AkihiroSuda/go-dag/scheduler"
)

g := &dag.Graph{
	Nodes: []dag.Node{0, 1, 2},
	Edges: []dag.Edge{
		{Depender: 2, Dependee: 0},
		{Depender: 2, Dependee: 1},
	},
}
concurrency := 0
scheduler.Execute(g, concurrency, func(n dag.Node) { buildStage(n) })
```

If this design is correct, I think we can vendor this package (or just copy it to `github.com/docker/docker/pkg/dag`)

### Determine Dockerfile DAG granularity

Alternatively, we could use fine-grained DAG like this, but I'm -1 ATM, because it is likely to cause implementation issue

![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/9248427/24951076/27fc4f12-1fae-11e7-88e8-0b63845e86fd.png)


### Refactor `builder` pkg to create DAG

My previous POC (https://github.com/docker/docker/pull/32402) was implemented in weird way:

- `builder/dockerfile/parser`(unchanged): parses `Dockerfile` text and returns parsed tree structure
- `builder/dockerfile/parallel`: re-parses output from `builder/dockerfile/parser`, and creates DAG

Re-parsing output from  `builder/dockerfile/parser` is likely to cause implementation issue; actually I forgot to implement support for `ARG`.

Rather, we should refactor `builder/dockerfile/parser` to emit DAG directly.

### Investigate other usecases of DAG

https://github.com/docker/docker/pull/32402#issuecomment-292254850

> The DAG based execution engine should be the new core of the builder, not only provide concurrent stage execution but concurrent build jobs, more efficient processing and cache reuse, cache export/import for DAG branches etc. In the same time, this core should be separated from the frontend(Dockerfile) logic to provide more options for declaring the build definition and also provide more extension points for others to reuse this solver.

### Investigate why `docker build` is slow

Storage driver seems being bottleneck, but haven't looked into this deeper

https://github.com/docker/docker/issues/9656
https://github.com/docker/docker/pull/32402#issuecomment-292313684
https://github.com/docker/docker/pull/32402#issuecomment-292888210

title: [Enhancement] add VxLAN port configuration support in "swarm init"
body:
Currently VxLAN default port is 4789 in swarm cluster. This value is not configurable at present.
This proposal will allow user to configure VxLAN  UDP port number during swarm init.  This way if anyone blocks VxLAN default port 4789 for swarm cluster, by changing default port to different value we will be able to still send/receive VxLAN packets on new port.
 

The change will be in 4 components. CLI, Moby, SwarmKit and  Libnetwork.
IANA procedures for each range in detail
the Well Known Ports, aka the System Ports, from 0-1023
the Registered Ports, aka the User Ports, from 1024-49151
the Dynamic Ports, aka the Private Ports, from 49152-65535

So we can allow range between 1024 to 49151

CLI command syntax :
 swarm init --vxlan-udp-port <1024-49151>
PS : swarm update will not have this option.  Only swarm init will have port config option.

cc : @thaJeztah @mavenugo @fcrisciani   @mark-church
Pls provide your inputs.

title: Limit restart exponential growth
body:
### Description

Currently, there is no way to limit exponential timeout increase in docker container restart policy. Though, in case I have container with short "active" lifetime and many reboots such approach will increase execution time dramatically.
I guess, it could be fixed by limiting the interval between checking container state(currently, it is growing exponentially).
Related issue, that was posted around 5 years ago: https://github.com/moby/moby/issues/41856

I am doing some test on health check in swarm or docker stand alone

My Dockerfile is this:
```
FROM ubuntu
COPY . /
HEALTHCHECK --interval=10s --timeout=3s CMD curl -f http://localhost:9000/ || exit 1
CMD [ "bash" , "start.sh" ]
```

start.sh script is:
```
#!/bin/bash
sudo apt-get update
apt-get install nc -y
sleep 40
nc -vvlnp 9000 >/dev/null
```

This simulate an application that takes 40 sec to start.
The container starts and fails after 39 seconds.
I expect that the docker engine will keep the container in starting until the first healthy check returns. 
So health check will be relevant for application that starts slow (Java/Rails...) and once starts health check returns fast  

I suggest to add to health check switch --terminate
So proper health check will be as follows:
 
```
HEALTHCHECK --interval=10s --timeout=3s --terminate=4m CMD curl -f http://localhost:9000/ || exit 1
```

Current status is that we cant use health check properly in short intervals on long starting applications

title: [RFC] Dropping legacy networking mode
body:
### Description

During the last couple weeks, we had a number of discussions on what should be done to remove legacy networking mode, and more particularly about legacy links. As there were many proposals made by various maintainers, this RFC try to summarize the various ideas floating around.

- [Goals](#goals)
- [Consensus](#consensus)
- [Points of contention](#points-of-contention)
    1. [Reimplement legacy links in terms of DNS records](#reimplement-legacy-links-in-terms-of-DNS-records)
    2. [Disable ICC altogether](#disable-ICC-altogether)
    3. [Enable ICC](#enable-ICC)
- [Deprecation plan](#deprecation-plan)

## <a name="goals" /> Goals

1. Deprecate and remove a feature marked as legacy for almost 10 years (finally!) ;
2. Reduce the complexity exposed to end-users and make it easier for them to transition from the default network to a custom network. In that regard, the default network should be a subset / "diminished version" of, or exactly the same as what custom networks provide. Currently, that's not the case because of the links feature having different semantics ;
3. Lastly, get rid of the current snowflake implementation used by the default network. This would reduce the complexity of libnetwork.

## <a name="consensus" /> Consensus

I think there're two things we all agree about:

1. `/etc/hosts`-based discovery should be let go and replaced by DNS-based discovery. It's recognized that this file isn't an API -- we don't mind breaking users who parse it ;
2. The current env vars mechanism is obsolete and should be removed. They're barely useful anyway since you've to parse `_NAME` env vars and know the port you want to reach to look up the right env vars:

```
$ docker run --rm -d --name=c0 -p 80:80 alpine top
$ docker run --rm -it --name=c1 --link=c0 alpine /bin/sh -c export
export C0_NAME='/c1/c0'
export C0_PORT='tcp://172.17.0.4:80'
export C0_PORT_80_TCP='tcp://172.17.0.4:80'
export C0_PORT_80_TCP_ADDR='172.17.0.4'
export C0_PORT_80_TCP_PORT='80'
export C0_PORT_80_TCP_PROTO='tcp'
```

Mostly as a side note (it probably requires a dedicated proposal), a replacement mechanism was briefly discussed. That mechanism could be used to solve other issues: #3778 (5th most upvoted networking issue, 25th overall) and #8427. This could take the form of:

1. A filesystem mount, allowing discoverability by walking the file tree. Another pro: it solves the notification issue (think Traefik use-case), and can be expanded to non-networking needs -- killing two birds with one stone. But there was some pushback on this design ;
2. Using SRV records. Cons:
  - The notification issue isn't solved ;
  - Thus (most probably) limited to ports discovery (eg. host port when publishing to an ephemeral port) ;
  - Ports don't have labels right now -- how to leverage RFC2782?

## <a name="points-of-contention" /> Points of contention

The current point of contention is about what the default bridge should look like, and what should be the semantics of links (on that network).

### <a name="reimplement-legacy-links-in-terms-of-dns-records" /> 1. Reimplement legacy links in terms of DNS records

The default network would be icc=false, and links would be used to declare which containers could reach each other.

From a user standpoint, the links semantics would still be unique to the default bridge, hardly hitting goals 2. and 3. However, we could change the semantics of links on custom networks to make it look like the current legacy semantics. But, this doesn't seem user-driven, making it hard to justify time investment and making the overall design more complex.

The new semantics would be:

- When icc=true, links are container-specific CNAME records ;
- When icc=false, same as icc=true plus they also define which containers can reach each other ;

From a technical standpoint, this is currently not easily feasible because non-legacy links are  implemented as container-specific CNAME records pointing to network-wide A records. When the DNS resolver is disabled, no A records are currently populated (**needs confirmation**).

### <a name="disable-icc-altogether" /> 2. Disable ICC altogether

Basically make the default bridge a north-south network -- ie. no inter-container connectivity, only a gateway to host's LAN/WAN. Legacy links should be replaced with custom networks, in line with what the docs currently advertise: https://docs.docker.com/network/links/.

There was some pushback on this idea as this would be a _massive_ breaking change -- this was already tried in the past and reverted.

### <a name="enable-icc" /> 3. Enable ICC

All containers connected to the default bridge can resolve and communicate with each other. No more legacy links -- links on the default bridge behave like on custom networks.

From a user standpoint, the default bridge network is just like any other bridge network. From a technical standpoint, no more snowflake implementation. This is probably the easiest solution, and the one which best fit goals 1-3.

This has the advantage of unifying Linux & Windows behaviors (the embedded DNS is enabled on Windows).

If users are unhappy about icc=true, we could still allow them to recreate the default bridge with whatever options they need, eg. like `docker_gwbridge`. There have been some discussions around unifying the way predefined networks are created / configured (eg. deprecate top-level daemon flags, unify the experience, etc...), so I'll keep those details for another proposal.

There was some pushback too but that's still too fuzzy for me, so I'll let anyone on the fence chime in. One potential blocker is that containers disconnected from Swarm networks end up being reattached to the default network -- but that looks like a silly bug warranting a proper fix (_I can't reproduce this issue_).

## <a name="deprecation-plan" /> Deprecation plan

This mostly depends on what alternative we adopt, but it'd be a variation of something like:

1. Show a WARNING on `docker create` / `docker run` whenever links are used on the default bridge network for a release or two ;
2. Disable legacy networking / links by default, and add a feature flag to re-enable them if needed ;
4. After a few releases, get totally rid of them.

**CWE:** CWE-909

### Description

Moby is an open source container framework developed by Docker Inc. that is distributed as Docker Engine, Mirantis Container Runtime, and various other downstream projects/products. A firewalld vulnerability affects Moby releases before 28.0.0. When firewalld reloads, Docker fails to re-create iptables rules that isolate bridge networks, allowing any container to access all ports on any other container across different bridge networks on the same host. This breaks network segmentation between containers that should be isolated, creating significant risk in multi-tenant environments. Only containers in --internal networks remain protected.
Workarounds include reloading firewalld and either restarting the docker daemon, re-creating bridge networks, or using rootless mode. Maintainers anticipate a fix for this issue in version 25.0.13.

```go
	b.ForEach(func(k, v []byte) error {

			defer func() {

title: Missing documentation: awslogs doesn't support AWS credentials files contrary to documentation
body:
It looks like awslogs doesn't support AWS credentials files contrary to [documentation](https://docs.docker.com/engine/reference/logging/awslogs/). The documentation says

```
You can provide these credentials with the AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, and AWS_SESSION_TOKEN environment variables, the default AWS shared credentials file (~/.aws/credentials of the root user)
```

First of all providing environment variables **and** credentials file is redundant because it caries same information. Secondly, hours of debugging indicate that Docker doesn't open `/root/.aws/credentials` at all which was verified with watching file events using `fatrace`.

As result `docker run` always fails with

```
Error response from daemon: Cannot start container case: Failed to initialize logging driver: NoCredentialProviders: no valid providers in chain
```

In order to make sure it's not me going crazy I wrote following simple application in Scala to doublecheck that AWS SDK does indeed works with credentials file

``` scala
val conf = ConfigFactory.load().getConfig("case")
val aws_region = RegionUtils.getRegion(conf.getString("aws_region"))

arr.add(event)

title: secrets: service update --secret-rm removes by "source", not "target"
body:
Doing more test on consistency, it looks like `--secret-rm` is using the wrong property for removing a secret;

To reproduce; create a secret, and a service that uses the same secret _twice_:

```bash
echo "world" | docker secret create hello

docker service create --name test --secret source=hello,target=world --secret source=hello,target=other-world nginx:alpine
```

Verify that the secret is used twice;

```bash
docker service inspect test --format '{{ json .Spec.TaskTemplate.ContainerSpec.Secrets}}' | jq
```

```json
[
  {
    "File": {
      "Name": "world",
      "UID": "0",
      "GID": "0",
      "Mode": 292
    },
    "SecretID": "jis2m9o0w5b2h4b1hu1ejjbwa",
    "SecretName": "hello"
  },
  {
    "File": {
      "Name": "other-world",
      "UID": "0",
      "GID": "0",
      "Mode": 292
    },
    "SecretID": "jis2m9o0w5b2h4b1hu1ejjbwa",
    "SecretName": "hello"
  }
]
```

Update the service, and remove a secret;

```bash
docker service update --secret-rm hello test
```

Both uses of the secret are removed;

```bash
docker service inspect test --format '{{ json .Spec.TaskTemplate.ContainerSpec.Secrets}}' | jq
null
```


The _target_ should be leading here, because a single secret can be used multiple times. This is also consistent with other options (e.g. `--mount-rm`)

title: Cancelling pulls
body:
### Description

When I ask the engine to pull an image via `/images/create` with `fromImage`, it streams back update events. If I close the HTTP connection, the pull is cancelled. As far as I know, there is no other way to cancel a pull.

Suppose I'm making a UI application (like Docker Desktop, which I'm a maintainer of), and I want to be able to cancel pulls initiated through the UI. Currently, that's difficult - it's necessary to maintain a list of open HTTP requests, with mechanisms for searching and closing them, effectively duplicating data that already exists in the engine. It would be better if we could cancel pulls without needing a reference to any open HTTP connections. This becomes more valuable in combination with #45434.

### Proposal

- Add a new API endpoint (dubious strawman suggestion: `/images/create/cancel`). If I post to this, passing a string in the same format as the `fromImage` parameter of `/images/create`, any matching in-progress pulls should abort.
- When a pull is cancelled, any currently open HTTP connections from matching calls to `/images/create` should emit a cancellation event, and then the connection should close.

### Related issues

- #45434

title: Docker transparent bridge
body:
When I use Docker networking, I usually miss one feature I would call `transparent bridge`. I've been enlightened by [Virtualbox bridged networking](https://www.virtualbox.org/manual/ch06.html#network_bridged), so the basic idea is excerpted as follows,

_With potential `transparent bridge`, Docker would use a `networking plugin` on your host system that filters data from your physical network adapter._ 

_This allows Docker to intercept data from the physical network and inject data into it, effectively creating a new network interface in software. When a container is using such a new software interface, it looks to the host system as though the container were physically connected to the interface using a network cable: the host can send data to the container through that interface and receive data from it._ 

_This means that you can set up routing or bridging between the container and the rest of your network._

For this to work, Docker needs a `networking plugin`  on the host system. Is this kind of plugin already existing or beneficial to make?

title: Better way to access the Engine API from a container
body:
Wouldn't it be nice if there existed an API access shim that one could use inside of a container without bind-mounting the socket and ensuring the client binary or libraries are compatible with the daemon you it happens to be talking to?

And, of course, it'd be critical to implement flexible access-control for what API calls are allowed.

One way to consider would be something as simple as:

``` shell
docker run --with-api-access-shim run <any_image> sh -c \
  "echo ps | socat - UNIX-CONNECT:/.docker.sock"
docker run --with-api-access-shim run <any_image> sh -c \
  "echo exec foo ls -la | socat - UNIX-CONNECT:/.docker.sock"
```

For those who need more, a shim shared library could be provided, with bindings for different languages.

title: Cluster defaults should not be overridden by swarm init
body:
`swarm init` creates a `ClusterSpec` and overwrites the cluster's object spec with this one. This means defaults such as certificate validity period and task history retention are under the client's control. They should be under SwarmKit's control instead.

`swarm init` should only change values from the defaults when a value is given through a flag. Currently, it appears to overwrite the whole spec with the client-side defaults when no flags are specified.

cc @aluzzardi @tonistiigi

title: more docs for ulimit nproc
body:
The `nproc` setting for `--ulimit` seems to be a special case in that it is limited per user (and per process). As such if you start up multiple containers using the same uid, they are limited by the same `nproc` value, for example:

```
docker run -d -u daemon --ulimit nproc=3 busybox top
docker run -d -u daemon --ulimit nproc=3 busybox top
docker run -d -u daemon --ulimit nproc=3 busybox top
docker run -d -u daemon --ulimit nproc=3 busybox top
```

The last `docker run` will fail since each container is using the same uid, and nproc for that user has been limited to 3... this is, unfortunately, how the system handles `nproc`

Some extra docs explaining this would be extremely helpful.

title: BLOCKER: Docker forgets about volumes created with plugin drivers after service restart
body:
I created a plugin volume driver that stores volumes on a remote file system. I then created a standalone volume with the following command:

```
$ docker volume create --driver=my-driver --name=geo-vol --opt BindDirectory=/work/docker-dev/volumes/geo-vol
geo-vol
```

And it works:

```
$ docker volume inspect geo-vol
[
    {
        "Name": "geo-vol",
        "Driver": "my-driver",
        "Mountpoint": "/work/docker-dev/volumes/geo-vol"
    }
]
$ ls -al /work/docker-dev/volumes/geo-vol/
total 0
drwxrwxrwx 1 vagrant vagrant  68 Feb  3 19:19 .
drwxrwxrwx 1 vagrant vagrant 680 Feb  3 19:19 ..
```

I am able to mount the volume in multiple containers and read and write data from all the containers. It's a great way to share data between containers! But there's a problem...

```
$ docker volume inspect geo-vol
[
    {
        "Name": "geo-vol",
        "Driver": "my-driver",
        "Mountpoint": "/work/docker-dev/volumes/geo-vol"
    }
]
$ sudo service docker restart
docker stop/waiting
docker start/running, process 27923
$ docker volume inspect geo-vol
Error response from daemon: no such volume
$ docker volume ls | grep geo
[no output]
```

When restarting, Docker completely forgot that the `geo-vol` volume exists. But my driver didn't. When trying to re-create it:

```
$ docker volume create --driver=my-driver --name=geo-vol --opt BindDirectory=/work/docker-dev/volumes/geo-vol
Error response from daemon: The volume geo-vol already exists.
```

Looking through the HTTP logs for my driver, it's definitely working correctly. When it works (before Docker restarts), `docker volume inspect` calls my driver (as it should) to get the volume path:

```
Pid-28176 Thread-2 localhost-socket - - [04/Feb/2016 03:00:18] "POST /VolumeDriver.Path HTTP/1.1" 200 62 '{"Name":"geo-vol"}'
```

But when it doesn't work (after Docker restarts), `docker volume inspect` doesn't bother to call my driver. So the problem is definitely that Docker has forgotten the volume during restart, not that my driver is doing something wrong.

This is a major blocker for us. I'm going to have to revert our Docker environment to using data volume containers until this is fixed. :-(

title: --cpus parameter can not be updated with Windows Server containers and docker inspect alwasy shows CpuCount equals 0
body:
Hello there,

I am running my test "microsoft/iis" container with following command with "--cpus 16" limitation:
```
docker run -d  --name gt_test_iis --cpus 16 microsoft/iis ping -t localhost
```

Looks like "--cpus" works fine and when I run my `simulate_cpu_load.ps1` script:
```
ForEach ($Number in 1..16){
   start-job -ScriptBlock{
      $result = 1; foreach ($number in 1..2147483647) {$result = $result * $number}
   }
}
```

I got only about 16% CPU on my 64 cpus virtual machine. 

When I wanted to change CPU limits online I tried `docker update` and got expected error (as --cpus flag is not described there https://docs.docker.com/engine/reference/commandline/update/#options):
```
PS> docker update --cpus 1 gt_test_iis
unknown flag: --cpus
See 'docker update --help'.
```

But on the API documentation page for "docker update" ( https://docs.docker.com/engine/api/v1.26/#operation/ContainerUpdate ) we have following option `CpuCount`, so from my understanding "docker update" should have "--cpus" parameter.

title: Avoiding private registry hostname in FROM directive of Dockerfile
body:
Say I have an image FOOBASE in a private registry (hostname:port PRIVREGHOSTNAME:5000)

I want to use this image in a Dockerfile for a new image FOONEW. Currently, it is done as follows:
# Dockerfile

FROM PRIVREGHOSTNAME:5000/FOOBASE
...

That is, the hostname of the private registry is in the Dockerfile.

Now say, I want to change the registries. I have to change the Dockerfile of FOOBASE, rebuild it, and rebuild the image FOONEW that depends on FOOBASE. Obviously, changing the Dockerfile is not desirable. The registry hostname should not be in the Dockerfile

Instead, a better solution is to define a new parameter --registry-url for docker build. E.g.,

docker build -t . --registry-url PRIVREGHOSTNAME:5000

So by default, the image referenced in Dockerfile is searched first in the registry-url and then in Dockerhub.

title: Feature Request: export more of the docker compose loader functions
body:
Can we export more of the docker/cli/compose/loader functions, to allow partial element decoding.

Reasoning:

we may not like the compose format that much, but it is an industry standard.  Now there are various docker provided libraries for unmarshalling the format, but the new compose library in the docker cli should likely become a standard.

Currently the only exported method is really the `Load()` method, which unmarshalls an entire compose file.  This is done because in legacy files, there was so much interconnection between the services, and the networks, that it was impossible to consider a single service or network on it's own.  Those reasons are no longer a problem now that the v3 files do away with the keys that required such interconnection (links, volumes_from.)
Or can we separate that loading code to it's own library (which would allow easy future deprecation anyway.)

Can we export any of the following functions, to give other software core decoding functionality?  

```
loadServices()
loadService()
loadNetworks()
loadVolumes()
loadSecrets()
```

If these methods were exported, then other projects could integrate the industry format into their own yml configurations, using the core code and not having to rewrite that code, or hack their formats to match the requirements for the Load() method.

The value gained would be easy reuse of the compose loader, to provide structs that can then be used to directly run client operations by mimicking the CLI.

title: Fast update service in loop broke swarm
body:
I used the following simple loop to make a few quick changes to an environment:

```
REG_URL=[docker_image_url]

for service in `docker service ls|grep '/image_name:'|awk {'print $1'}`
do
  docker service update $service --image $REG_URL
  docker service update $service --env-add LOG_ENTRIES_KEY=ABCD1234
done
```

After running this script, I was no longer able to communicate from the manager node to any swarm node, getting a timeout error for simple commands like `docker service rm`

The same script without adding another environment variable works fine and causes no issues.

I suspect that running the update service with two flags on one command would have worked fine; although I didn't try, running it as two commands should not cause nodes to become unavailable.

Perhaps something is causing a problem if the first update command hasn't completed on the backend while the second one attempts to run?

I was only able to recover the swarm by running `docker swarm leave` on each node, and readding them..

title: Include More Information in Daemon Logs
body:
Recently at work was prompted at work to tail the docker daemon logs to investigate an condition (which was sorted out) I had the daemon running on `debug` mode and I found some information missing that could have been useful in debugging, to explain what I mean let me elaborate: 

Our Docker use case can be termed as command and control where we have a set of master instances talking to a bunch of minions who instruct the minions to perform image/container management (pull, push, start, kill) to aid, debug and potentially leave a log-trail of command origin it will be very useful to list the source of the command to the docker daemon for example current daemon logs look like:

![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/311217/4878297/474f709e-6307-11e4-8604-ddd648c1bc29.png)

These log fragments provide what command was executed but does not provide clue about its origin as in whether it came from localhost or remote host. I also saw that the future releases will contain a enhanced and a more parsable log format #8761 which is awesome but I feel that providing the source where the command came from will be useful as well in establishing an log-trail about container management.

title: Support `docker run --rm=5m (or --rm-after=5m)` to facilitate running docker on something like coreos+fleet
body:
When running a daemon on coreos using fleetctl it can be cumbersome to try and manage cleaning up the leftover containers after the service has been terminated or migrated to a new host.

Using `docker run --rm` does not work well since it would remove the container any time the service is restarted by either user intervention or a crash. Instead having a way to cleanup once the service is gone would be best (perhaps this should be a fleet feature instead/as well), but having the option to remove the container after a period of non-use would be handy.

Implementation wise, once container exists sleep for time period, awaken see that container has been idle for >= sleep time, and remove. Otherwise, if it was reactivated it should not removed.
